headline: Google now lets adults in the US run apps they built with AI on their own Android phones through Google Play, without publishing them to the public store.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a Google change that opens native Android app-building to ordinary people, though it starts in the US only and the sharing features are still to come.
importance_line: Hobbyists and other non-programmers can run apps they made with AI on their own phones without a public release, but at first it is for US adults only and the apps must still follow Play policies.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Google announced on Tuesday that Android owners in the US aged 18 and over can build an app in Google AI Studio, where a person describes an app to an AI that writes it, known as vibe coding, and launch it privately on their own device through Google Play. Such apps stay out of Play search and listings, must still follow Play policies, and Google says sharing with a small circle of trusted friends is planned for the months ahead.
notes: Read in full on TechCrunch. Google's statement was given at a press briefing and quoted by TechCrunch (Sam Bright, vice president and general manager of Google Play and Developer Ecosystem).
